Unit 9 • SL

Computer Systems

Introduction

What really happens inside a computer when you run a program?

This unit focuses on how computer systems execute instructions at hardware level. You will study CPU components, memory hierarchy, instruction-cycle behavior, secondary storage choices, and cloud service models.

You will describe how the ALU, CU, registers, and buses interact; explain RAM/ROM/cache purposes; describe the fetch-decode-execute cycle; describe internal and external secondary storage; and describe SaaS, PaaS, and IaaS cloud services.

CPU architecture

The CPU is a coordinated system of components, not a single block.

  • ALU: arithmetic and logic operations.
  • CU: control signals and instruction coordination.
  • Registers: fast temporary state (PC, MAR, MDR, ACC, IR).
  • Buses: address, data, and control communication paths.

Primary memory hierarchy

Speed, cost, and capacity are balanced across memory types.

  • Registers/Cache: fastest, smallest, closest to CPU.
  • RAM: volatile working memory for active programs.
  • ROM: non-volatile firmware/boot memory.

Instruction execution

Every program runs through the fetch-decode-execute cycle repeatedly.

  • Fetch: retrieve instruction from memory.
  • Decode: interpret opcode and operands.
  • Execute: perform operation and update state.

Persistent storage and cloud

Systems combine local storage choices with cloud service models.

  • Secondary storage: SSD, HDD, flash, optical, NAS.
  • Cloud models: SaaS, PaaS, IaaS.
  • Key trade-offs: performance, cost, control, and scalability.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
ALUCPU unit that performs arithmetic and logical operations.
Control UnitCPU unit that manages instruction sequencing and control signals.
PC / MAR / MDR / ACC / IRCore CPU registers used to track instruction addresses, memory access, and intermediate results.
Address/Data/Control busCommunication channels for addresses, payload data, and system control signals.
RAMVolatile primary memory used for active programs and data.
ROMNon-volatile memory storing firmware and startup routines.
Cache (L1/L2/L3)Small high-speed memory layers used to reduce average access latency.
Fetch-Decode-ExecuteThe repeating instruction cycle used by the CPU to run programs.
Secondary storagePersistent non-volatile storage for long-term data retention.
SaaS / PaaS / IaaSCloud service models defining different responsibility boundaries.

Common Misconceptions

RAM and storage are the same

RAM is volatile working memory; storage is persistent long-term data retention.

PC holds the current instruction

PC normally points to the next instruction to fetch.

Cloud means no physical hardware

Cloud services run on real physical infrastructure in data centers.

Real-World Uses

  • Selecting hardware for school labs and media workstations
  • Diagnosing system bottlenecks in CPU/memory workflows
  • Choosing SSD/HDD/NAS storage strategies
  • Planning SaaS vs PaaS vs IaaS service adoption
  • Explaining how low-level execution supports high-level software

Think Deeper

"Where should control sit: local hardware or remote cloud infrastructure?" System design decisions affect performance, cost, privacy, and operational dependency.
